items.title: Charles McPherson interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: here we are, we’ve auditioned to get in this man’s band, and we’re in his band now

ctx.x: Well I knew him as Noel. Oh, okay. All right. Now he was just a folk singer singing, playing his guitar, and then we had this jam session in the afternoon, and Bill Cosby or people like that or even Bob Dylan would be at some coffee house across the street, and everybody was just like struggling nonentities basically, really. And so in the afternoon we’d have these sessions. And Mingus came by one afternoon because he was in need of an alto player and a trumpet player. And we were recommended by Yusef, who worked…

plucks them out with his hands. And so Lonnie and I, we looked at that and here we are, we’ve auditioned to get in this man’s band, and we’re in his band now, and there he is over there tearing the piano up, three hundred pounds. We were like 20 years old, 19, 20. And it was like oh, man, we work for somebody like this. And these gangsters, this just shows you the power of psychosis. I don’t care who anybody is, if you act, if you seem to be more crazy, crazier than they are, it’s awesome. And everybody respects…

items.title: Charles McPherson interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 9, 2024 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: And it was basically inspired by my involvement with Paul Chambers, Barry Harris, Billy Higgins, and Lonnie Hillyer, a trumpet player, and myself. We had a gig

ctx.x: Was this a conscious decision to —

Yeah. It was. Yeah. Because most of the time you’re going to get the trumpet or the saxophone or the horns play first. So just for the sake of variation and, you know, to add a different flavor, you know I like to have the bass or piano player play first, not only in clubs but on records as well. And it was written to be their feature you know. It was written to be their feature. And it was basically inspired by my involvement with Paul Chambers, Barry Harris, Billy Higgins, and Lonnie Hillyer, a trumpet player,…
Indeed. And I’m picturing you, were you sitting at the piano laboriously writing out this [scats]-type line?
